assessments.reason: At stages 0, 5, 8 and 30, the established p licenses the inclusive disjunction, which supplies the antecedent for the next p. At 2, 15, 17, 22 and 24, d and p are combined and used jointly. Every other stage derives its m from p and the next p from that m.

The rewrite uses the disjunction itself to reach p7 and p23. At stages 11, 15 and 19 it forms the specified conjunction and derives the next p from it. At all other stages both implications are applied in order through the specified m.

Stages 4, 6, 10, 15 and 20 each introduce an inclusive disjunction from p and use it to infer the next p. Stages 11, 13, 17, 24, 26, 27, 29 and 31 each combine the given d with the established p before using their conjunction. Every remaining stage asserts both steps through m.

Stages 9, 11, 16 and 22 introduce the disjunction from the known disjunct and apply its conditional. Stages 13, 14 and 15 each form and use a separate conjunction, as do 20 and 26. The other stages retain the two directed implications through their respective m.
